50887628.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human BRD9 by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Instruments, Worcestershire, U.K.) at 25 °C. The protein (BRD9) was dialyzed against 20 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, pH 7.5, and concentrated to 100 μM. The compound (13-d) was dissolved in DMSO and diluted to 10 mM in the same buffer. The protein was loaded into the sample cell (200 μL), and the compound was loaded into the syringe (250 μL). The titration consisted of 20 injections of 2 μL each, with a 120 s spacing between injections. The stirring speed was set to 300 rpm. A blank experiment was performed by titrating the compound into buffer alone. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (MicroCal) with a one-site binding model. The binding constant (K), enthalpy change (ΔH), and stoichiometry (n) were determined from the fit. The binding free energy (ΔG) was calculated from the equation ΔG = -RT ln K, and the entropy change (ΔS) was calculated from the equation ΔG = ΔH - TΔS. The data are presented as the mean ± SD of at least two independent experiments.
original_paragraph.Figure 6 caption: Figure 6. ITC data for 13-d with BRPF1. The figure shows raw binding heats for each injection (upper panel) as well as normalized binding enthalpies and a nonlinear least-squares fit to a single binding site model. The fit revealed K_D = 40 nM, ΔH = -11.7 kcal mol⁻¹, and TΔS = -1.87 kcal mol⁻¹.

assay_conditions.buffer_composition: 20 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT
assay_conditions.control_method: Titration of compound into buffer alone

50887631.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human BRPF2 by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Instruments, Worcestershire, U.K.) at 25 °C. The protein (BRPF1, BRPF2, or BRPF3) was dialyzed against 20 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, pH 7.5, and concentrated to 100 μM. The ligand (13-d) was dissolved in DMSO and diluted in the same buffer to a final concentration of 100 μM. The protein was loaded into the sample cell (200 μL), and the ligand was loaded into the syringe (250 μL). The experiment consisted of 20 injections of 2 μL each, with a 120 s spacing between injections. The stirring speed was set to 300 rpm. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (MicroCal) with a one-site binding model. The control experiment involved titrating the ligand into buffer alone to correct for the heat of dilution. The binding affinity (Kd), enthalpy change (ΔH), and stoichiometry (n) were determined from the fitted isotherm. The data for 13-d with BRPF1 are shown in Figure 6. The ITC data for 13-d with BRPF2 and BRPF3 are shown in Supporting Information, Figure S3.
original_paragraph.Figure 6 caption: Figure 6. ITC data for 13-d with BRPF1. The figure shows raw binding heats for each injection (upper panel) as well as normalized binding enthalpies and a nonlinear least-squares fit to a single binding site model. The fit revealed Kd = 40 nM, ΔH = −11.7 kcal mol−1, and TΔS = −1.87 kcal mol−1.
original_paragraph.Table 4: ITC data showed that 13-d bound the BRD of BRPF1 with an equilibrium dissociation constant, Kd, of 40 nM and an enthalpy change, ΔH, of −11.7 kcal mol−1 (Table 4, Figure 6). Additional ITC studies showed 13-d bound the BRD of BRD1 with a Kd of 210 nM, whereas binding to BRPF3 and BRD9 was weaker (Table 4; Supporting Information, Figure S3).

assay_conditions.buffer_composition: 20 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT
assay_conditions.control_method: Titration of ligand into buffer alone to correct for the heat of dilution
